t: Multi-Source Evidence Combiner: a plain-language overview
title: Multi-Source Evidence Combiner: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Multi-Source Evidence Combiner does and why archives need it. A multi-source evidence combiner takes many sources' word on one question and produces one careful answer. It weighs each source by reliability, discounts sources that just copied each other, and reports where they agree and where they fight. Many voices become one honest verdict.
demo:
# Multi-Source Evidence Combiner - runnable demo (JAH-ATK198-000001)
RANK = 1
SIG = False
EV = [('s1', 'yes', 0.9, None), ('s2', 'yes', 0.8, 's1'), ('s3', 'no', 0.7, None), ('s4', 'yes', 0.6, None)]  # (source, claim_yes_no, reliability, copies_from_or_None)
weights = {}
for src, claim, rel, copied in EV:
    w = rel * (0.4 if copied else 1.0)  # dependence discount
    weights[src] = (claim, w, copied)
yes = sum(w for c, w, _ in weights.values() if c == "yes")
no = sum(w for c, w, _ in weights.values() if c == "no")
verdict = "YES" if yes > no else "NO" if no > yes else "TIE"
print("verdict: %s  (yes-weight %.2f vs no-weight %.2f)" % (verdict, yes, no))
for src, (claim, w, copied) in weights.items():
    print("  %-6s claims %-3s weight=%.2f%s" % (src, claim, w, " [discounted: copies %s]" % copied if copied else ""))
if RANK >= 2:
    dissent = [s for s, (c, _, _) in weights.items() if (c == "yes") != (verdict == "YES")]
    print("dissenters:", dissent if dissent else "none")
if RANK >= 3:
    print("effective independent weight: %.2f" % (yes + no))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-EVD-" + "JAH-ATK198-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK198-000001", "OK")
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Multi-Source Evidence Combiner works: the deep tour
title: How the Multi-Source Evidence Combiner works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Multi-Source Evidence Combiner does and why archives need it. Real combiners use weighted voting where weights reflect source reliability and independence: dependent sources (one citing another, shared underlying data) are discounted so they cannot stuff the ballot. Agreement metrics (Fleiss' kappa, consensus ratios) quantify how much sources concur, and conflicts are preserved in the output rather than averaged away. The verdict carries its margin, its dissenters, and the weight ledger behind it. Advanced systems model source dependence as a graph, apply Bayesian updating with explicit priors, and detect correlated errors (all sources repeating one wrong wire report). Quality is measured by verdict accuracy on questions with known answers and by calibration of reported confidence. The limits are questions where all sources share one flawed origin — the combiner reports the dependence structure honestly so the verdict's fragility is visible, because a unanimous echo chamber is not evidence.

RANK = 1
SIG = False
EV = [('s1', 'yes', 0.9, None), ('s2', 'yes', 0.8, 's1'), ('s3', 'no', 0.7, None), ('s4', 'yes', 0.6, None)]  # (source, claim_yes_no, reliability, copies_from_or_None)
weights = {}
for src, claim, rel, copied in EV:
    w = rel * (0.4 if copied else 1.0)  # dependence discount
    weights[src] = (claim, w, copied)
yes = sum(w for c, w, _ in weights.values() if c == "yes")
no = sum(w for c, w, _ in weights.values() if c == "no")
verdict = "YES" if yes > no else "NO" if no > yes else "TIE"
print("verdict: %s  (yes-weight %.2f vs no-weight %.2f)" % (verdict, yes, no))
for src, (claim, w, copied) in weights.items():
    print("  %-6s claims %-3s weight=%.2f%s" % (src, claim, w, " [discounted: copies %s]" % copied if copied else ""))
if RANK >= 2:
    dissent = [s for s, (c, _, _) in weights.items() if (c == "yes") != (verdict == "YES")]
    print("dissenters:", dissent if dissent else "none")
if RANK >= 3:
    print("effective independent weight: %.2f" % (yes + no))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-EVD-" + "JAH-ATK198-000013")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK198-000013", "OK")

description: Production: how the Multi-Source Evidence Combiner runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real combiners use weighted voting where weights reflect source reliability and independence: dependent sources (one citing another, shared underlying data) are discounted so they cannot stuff the ballot. Agreement metrics (Fleiss' kappa, consensus ratios) quantify how much sources concur, and conflicts are preserved in the output rather than averaged away. The verdict carries its margin, its dissenters, and the weight ledger behind it.

t: The Multi-Source Evidence Combiner at archive scale
title: The Multi-Source Evidence Combiner at archive scale
description: Production: how the Multi-Source Evidence Combiner runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real combiners use weighted voting where weights reflect source reliability and independence: dependent sources (one citing another, shared underlying data) are discounted so they cannot stuff the ballot. Agreement metrics (Fleiss' kappa, consensus ratios) quantify how much sources concur, and conflicts are preserved in the output rather than averaged away. The verdict carries its margin, its dissenters, and the weight ledger behind it. Advanced systems model source dependence as a graph, apply Bayesian updating with explicit priors, and detect correlated errors (all sources repeating one wrong wire report). Quality is measured by verdict accuracy on questions with known answers and by calibration of reported confidence. The limits are questions where all sources share one flawed origin — the combiner reports the dependence structure honestly so the verdict's fragility is visible, because a unanimous echo chamber is not evidence.
